plan.title: Impact of Horizontal Velocity on Landing Stability
plan.hypothesis: Increasing the initial horizontal velocity (vx) will increase the lateral displacement at touchdown, potentially exceeding the safe contact velocity thresholds.

scenarios.label: Low Drift
scenarios.rationale: Tests a small negative horizontal velocity to see if the controller can correct minor drift.

scenarios.label: Moderate Drift
scenarios.rationale: Tests a moderate positive horizontal velocity to observe the controller's response to significant lateral momentum.

scenarios.label: High Drift
scenarios.rationale: Tests a high horizontal velocity near the edge of the allowed range to determine the limits of the PPO/PD controller's correction capability.

cases.label: Reference
cases.rationale: Nominal starting conditions; the same seeds are used for every case.

cases.label: High Drift
cases.rationale: Tests a high horizontal velocity near the edge of the allowed range to determine the limits of the PPO/PD controller's correction capability.

interpretation.headline: Increased horizontal velocity impacts PPO landing stability

findings.hypothesis: Small negative drift may challenge the controller's ability to maintain stability
Moderate positive drift may exceed the correction capabilities of the PPO controller
High horizontal velocity likely prevents successful landing with the PPO controller

interpretation.next_question: How does varying the descent speed (vy) affect the PPO controller's ability to compensate for moderate horizontal drift?

question: Find how increasing sideways drift affects landing. Keep altitude and descent speed the same.
